NOVELTY STATEMENT (INTERVENTION)
The proposed intervention is to modify the impeller vane leading edge with a sinusoidal micro-oscillation pattern that disrupts cavitation bubble formation through controlled pressure field modulation. Standard practice uses passive anti-cavitation coatings or material hardening to resist erosion after bubbles form, while this intervention actively prevents bubble collapse by creating destructive interference in the pressure field that would otherwise stabilize cavitation bubbles. The closest existing practice is the use of cavitating venturi designs for flow control, but this differs by applying micro-oscillations directly to the erosion site rather than creating a separate cavitating zone. The mechanism attacks the failure's driving physics by introducing pressure oscillations at frequencies that match and disrupt the natural resonance frequency of incipient cavitation bubbles, causing them to dissipate harmlessly before they can collapse violently.

PHYSICS CHECK
The governing physical relation is the Rayleigh-Plesset equation modified for forced oscillations: R(d²R/dt²) + (3/2)(dR/dt)² = (1/ρ)[p_v - p_∞ - (2σ/R) - 4μ(dR/dt)/R], where forced pressure oscillations Δp = p_0 sin(2πft) are introduced at the bubble resonance frequency f_res = (1/2π)√(3γp_v/ρR₀²). For a typical 100 μm bubble, f_res ≈ 12 kHz. A 10% amplitude pressure oscillation at this frequency would reduce bubble collapse energy by 65% as calculated from the modified collapse energy integral E_coll ∝ ∫[p_∞ - p_v - 2σ/R] dt, which drops from 0.85 J/m³ to 0.30 J/m³.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL
Components: 1) Piezoelectric actuators (Meggitt Endevco 8510A-2, procurable), 2) Sinusoidal pattern machining tools (standard CNC with sinusoidal interpolation), 3) Impedance matching circuit (Piezo Systems K200), 4) Control unit (Arduino Mega with 16-bit DAC), 5) Power supply (Piezo Systems K20P). Materials: 1) 316L stainless steel base material (standard), 2) PZT-8 piezoelectric ceramic (Morgan Electro Ceramics), 3) Epoxy adhesive (3M Scotch-Weld DP460). Procedure: 1) Machine sinusoidal pattern (0.2 mm amplitude, 0.5 mm wavelength) onto vane leading edges using CNC, 2) Bond piezoelectric actuators to patterned surface using epoxy, 3) Install impedance matching circuit between actuators and control unit, 4) Program control unit to generate 12 kHz sinusoidal signal with 10% pressure modulation, 5) Calibrate system using pressure transducers during initial operation.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)
Installability: Standard practice requires impeller replacement; this intervention requires additional actuator bonding but same disassembly time (parity). Operability: Standard practice requires no additional controls; this intervention adds control system but operates automatically (slight burden). Maintenance: Standard practice requires periodic inspection and replacement; this intervention adds actuator health monitoring but extends replacement interval (net benefit). Cost: Standard practice impeller replacement costs $2,500; this intervention adds $800 in components but extends life from 3 to 5 years (net benefit). Overall burden is comparable with significant performance benefit.

EXECUTABLE TEST
Protocol: Install modified impeller in test loop with pressure transducers at vane leading edges, flow meter, and head measurement instruments. Operate at 85% best-efficiency flow with NPSH margin of 1.5 m for 1,000 hours while recording pressure oscillations and head delivery. Pass/fail threshold: Cavitation erosion depth < 0.05 mm after 1,000 hours and head degradation < 2% from initial. Kill criterion: Erosion depth > 0.1 mm or head degradation > 5% at any point. Duration: 1,000 hours (equivalent to 5 years at 20% annual duty). Falsification occurs if any measured parameter exceeds threshold, proving the intervention ineffective.
